text:
I need to send a quarterly update to our investors. I'm the founder of a scheduling app for physical therapy clinics. We have 6 people.

Numbers for the quarter:
- Monthly recurring revenue is $41,000, the same as three months ago.
- We added 9 clinics and lost 4. One of the 4 was our largest customer, a 12-clinic chain that paid $5,500 a month. They moved to the scheduler built into their electronic records system.
- We have $480,000 in the bank and lose about $44,000 a month.
- Clinics that use our automatic text reminders have a no-show rate of 7%, against 13% before they started.
- I didn't send updates for the last two quarters.
- Next month we start selling the reminder feature on its own for $150 a month.

Under 500 words. It goes to 11 investors.

Before I write, here's the argument the update has to make, plus a few questions. With a runway this short and two missed updates, investors will read this closely, so I'd rather fill in real facts than guess.

**What the update has to argue**

- **Main point:** Flat revenue hides a real finding. The part customers value most is the reminders, and it can be sold to clinics that will never buy our scheduler. Next month's launch tests that, and we'll know the answer well before the money runs out.
- **Facts it rests on:** We added 9 clinics and lost 4, so we grew by 5. Losing the $5,500 account was the only reason MRR stayed at $41K: everything else grew by about $5,500 a month. Clinics using reminders went from a 13% no-show rate to 7%, close to half. We have about 11 months of cash, which takes us to around October 2027.
- **What links them:** If clinics are moving to the schedulers built into their records systems, a product that works alongside those systems turns that threat into the market.
- **What investors will object to:**
  1. "If the records systems can take your biggest customer, they can take the rest."
  2. "At $150 a month, it takes about 37 reminder customers to replace that one account, and about 290 to cover the burn."
  3. "Why did we hear nothing for six months?"

**Questions** (most important first)

1. **Does the standalone reminder product work with clinics that schedule in their records system?** If yes, which systems? Do you have any early interest: pilots, a waitlist, or clinics that have asked for it? This is the main answer to objection 1.
2. **What will you commit to, and by when?** For example, a number of reminder customers by a set date, and what you'll do if you miss it (cut costs, change direction, raise money). With 11 months of cash, investors will look for this.
3. **Are you raising money, and is there anything you want from these 11 investors?** For example, introductions to clinic chains, or help with a bridge round.
4. **How many of your current clinics use a records system that has its own scheduler?** In other words, how many customers face the same risk as the chain you lost? If you don't know, that's fine. I'll leave it out.
5. **The missed updates:** do you want to say why in one line, and commit to sending one every quarter from now on?

Answer whichever you can. I won't invent anything you leave blank.

1. I don't know which records systems it works with. Early interest: 6 clinics have said they'll buy it on its own when it launches December 1.

2. I haven't set a target for reminder customers or a plan for missing one. What I can commit to: an update in the first week of every quarter, with the next one on January 7, and a monthly one-page set of numbers for any investor who asks.

3. I don't know about raising yet. What I want from them is 20 minutes on the phone and introductions to clinic chains.

4. Two other customers use the same records system as the chain that left. Together they pay $3,800 a month. I can't promise they won't leave the same way.

5. Yes. The numbers were flat and I didn't want to send bad news. There was no other reason. And yes, commit to quarterly.

I've written it so the bad news comes first and is stated plainly, and the reminder launch is presented as a test that's starting, not a fix that's already working. The draft is about 430 words.

<final_document>
Subject: Quarterly update: flat revenue, a lost customer, and a December 1 launch

Hi all,

First, an apology. This is my first update in six months. The numbers were flat and I didn't want to send bad news. There was no other reason, and it was the wrong call. From now on you'll get an update in the first week of every quarter, starting January 7. If you'd like a one-page set of numbers every month, reply and I'll add you.

**The numbers**

- Monthly recurring revenue: $41,000, the same as three months ago.
- Clinics: added 9, lost 4.
- Cash: $480,000 in the bank, losing about $44,000 a month. That's roughly 11 months of runway.

Revenue stayed flat because of one loss. Our largest customer, a 12-clinic chain paying $5,500 a month, moved to the scheduler built into their electronic records system. Growth everywhere else added about $5,500 a month, which only covered that loss.

**The risk I can't rule out**

Two other customers use the same records system as the chain that left. Together they pay $3,800 a month, and I can't promise they won't leave the same way. If they did, monthly revenue would fall to $37,200 and our runway would shrink to about 10 months.

**What's working**

Clinics that use our automatic text reminders have a no-show rate of 7%, down from 13% before they started. That cuts missed appointments almost in half, and for a clinic a missed appointment is lost revenue. Of everything we offer, this is where the value is clearest.

**What we're doing about it**

On December 1 we start selling the reminders on their own for $150 a month, so a clinic can buy them without switching schedulers. Six clinics have already told us they'll buy at launch. That's a start, not proof. At $150 a month it would take about 37 customers to replace the account we lost. I also haven't yet confirmed which records systems the standalone product works with. In the January 7 update I'll report how many clinics have bought it.

I haven't decided whether to raise money. With about 11 months of cash, I'd value your view on that.

**What I'm asking for**

1. **20 minutes on the phone.** I'd like to hear how you read these numbers and what you'd do in my position.
2. **Introductions to physical therapy clinic chains.** One chain brought us 12 clinics at once, so chains are the fastest way to grow both the scheduler and the reminders.

Reply to this email and I'll send times.

Thanks,
</final_document>

A few things to check before you send:

- **Sign-off:** I left your name and company name off because you didn't give them. Add them after "Thanks."
- **Figures I worked out:**
  - The runway figures: $480K ÷ $44K ≈ 11 months. If the two at-risk customers left, the monthly loss would rise to about $47.8K, giving about 10 months.
  - The 37 customers: $5,500 ÷ $150.
- **A promise I added:** saying you'll report standalone sales in the January 7 update is my wording. Cut it if you don't want to be held to it.
- **A number I left out:** covering the whole $44K monthly loss with reminders alone would take about 290 customers. Some of your investors will work that out themselves. If you'd rather say it before they do, add it after the "37 customers" sentence.
- **What would make this stronger:** a target for reminder customers by a set date, and what you'll do if you miss it. Investors with 11 months of runway in front of them will be looking for one. I didn't invent one, but if you set it before January 7, put it in that update.
